dissents.topic: Severity of the flattenRef termination / recursion-guard concern

positions.position: P0 — no stated invariant or termination proof for the new parent branch; the seen.parent recursion lacks an analogous guard to seen.ref = null.
P0 — no proven termination function; the seen.ref = null sentinel is a smuggled goto and seen.parent is never nulled.
P1 — flattenRef does three jobs glued together with mutation and recursive re-entry; should be a single stateless transform.
P0 — finalize complects five transformations on a shared mutable map; the control flow is where the bug will live.
P1 — wrong boundary: flattenRef owns four responsibilities operating order-dependently on the same object.
Not flagged as a termination/recursion issue per se; concerns expressed as bad taste / model-missing rather than soundness.

dissents.topic: Severity of JSON.stringify being used as the dedup equality primitive

positions.position: P0 — asymptotically wrong; quadratic-in-subtree-size on the hot path; must be replaced.
P0 — easy-not-simple; place-oriented thinking; heisenbug on first key-order difference.
P0 — using JSON.stringify as an equality relation is a vibe, not reasoning; refuse the change.
P1 — leaky abstraction; the predicate must be stated and implemented as a documented helper.
P1 — too clever; track ownership of keys at assignment time so dedup becomes set-difference.
P1 — wrong tool; slow, allocating, order-sensitive; symptom of a missing 'where did this property come from' field.

dissents.topic: Severity and interpretation of the overrideCount 6 -> 12 test change

positions.position: P1 — silent user-visible contract change; either restore gating or document the new contract.
P1 — test was literally titled 'do not run on references'; pick one — regression or intended — and write the commit message.
P0 — silent semantic change shipped under a refactor; the test name is now a lie or the contract has changed; must be made explicit or reverted.
P1 — behavior change disguised as a test update; running override twice (once on parent, once on child-refinement) may not be what callers want.
P1 — public-facing contract change for override callbacks; document or revert.
P2 — magic number change hides a semantic shift; deserves a comment or a guard against double-firing.

dissents.topic: How to evaluate the fileProcessor refactor (hoist shared props out of anyOf)

positions.position: P2 GOOD-TASTE — eliminates real duplication; should land as its own patch.
P2 — genuinely simpler decomposition; worth a one-line invariant comment to prevent regression.
P2 — clean composition win; downstream tooling walking anyOf naively may regress; needs a comment on merge semantics.
P1 — correct for draft 2020-12 but lacks the literate comment distinguishing spec semantics across targets (07/04, OpenAPI 3.0) that flattenRef handles.
P1 — weakens each anyOf branch's standalone postcondition; LSP-style weakening if branches are documented as standalone schemas.
P1 — relocates shared properties with no spec for the resulting shape; snapshot equality is not a proof.

issues.description: Recursive flattenRef has no stated invariant or termination proof for the new parent branch
issues.detail: The rewritten flattenRef has two recursive call sites: flattenRef(ref) at the top and flattenRef(seen.parent) when seen.parent !== ref. The original code guaranteed termination by setting seen.ref = null before recursing; the new parent branch has no analogous guard. If seen.parent forms a cycle through another node's parent chain that has not yet had its ref nulled, this recurses indefinitely. State the invariant ('each node is flattened at most once') and prove termination explicitly, or add a visited-set / second sentinel.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as the equality primitive for property de-duplication inside finalize
issues.detail: Two new blocks in flattenRef decide whether to delete a key via JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key]). JSON.stringify is order-sensitive on objects, lossy for undefined, throws on cycles, mis-handles NaN/Infinity/BigInt, and allocates two strings per comparison. It is called twice per key, inside flattenRef, which is invoked for every entry in ctx.seen — at minimum O(N * K * S) and on the hot JSON-schema-generation path. Use a documented structural-equality predicate, or track at assignment time which keys came from inheritance versus the child so dedup becomes set-difference.

issues.description: finalize/flattenRef complects four-to-five transformations on a shared mutable schema with no stated invariants between phases
issues.detail: flattenRef performs (1) ref-chain flattening with recursion guard, (2) inherit-from-ref plus child-wins merge, (3) parent-only key stripping on a 'refinement' branch, (4) $ref-extraction dedup via JSON.stringify equality, and (5) a second $ref propagation pass for seen.parent !== ref. These are sequenced by side effect on the same map and gated by ad-hoc conditions ('if isParentRef' vs 'if refSchema.$ref' vs 'if seen.parent && seen.parent !== ref'). Compute the final schema as a pure function of (own props, inherited props, parent ref, child overrides) and assign once at the end; otherwise the next maintainer cannot reason about which phase a bug lives in.

issues.description: Seen.ref / Seen.parent semantics are undocumented and overlap dangerously
issues.detail: The Seen interface now has two near-identical fields: ref (inherit-from / processor-set / null sentinel for 'already processed') and parent (clone-chain parent). The relationship between them is encoded in conditional logic across process() and finalize() (e.g. 'if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent', 'isParentRef = _zod.parent === ref', 'seen.parent !== ref'). ref now encodes three meanings — absent, in-progress-sentinel (null), and pointing-to-a-schema — while parent uses undefined for absence. Specify the legal states of each field, the invariant after process() returns, and ideally replace with a discriminated/named state (e.g. inheritFrom / cloneParent / visited).

issues.description: play.ts committed as a debug scratchpad with a relative source import
issues.detail: play.ts switched from `import * as z from 'zod/v4'` to `import * as z from './packages/zod/src/index.js'` and contains hand-written console.log probes for the very bug being fixed. It is the author's working scratchpad, not part of a shipped patch. Revert play.ts to its prior form, move it to tests/repros/ as a real test, or drop it from the PR.

issues.description: Single PR bundles three unrelated changes (parent-tracking fix, fileProcessor refactor, mini parent:true enablement)
issues.detail: The diff contains (1) the parent metadata tracking rewrite in to-json-schema.ts plus the wrapper-id test, (2) the fileProcessor hoist-shared-props refactor and snapshot update, and (3) the mini/schemas.ts parent:true enablement. They have independent justifications, independent risk, and independent bisect value. Split into separate patches so each can be reviewed and reverted on its own merit.

issues.description: overrideCount test expectation doubled from 6 to 12 while the test title still asserts 'do not run on references'
issues.detail: The previous finalize gated `ctx.override(...)` with `if (!seen.isParent)`; the new code removes that guard, and the test was updated from toBe(6) to toBe(12). The test is literally titled 'override: do not run on references' — doubling the override count is the exact failure mode that test was written to catch. This is a user-visible contract change for anyone who registered an override callback expecting leaf-only invocation. Either restore the gating, update the test title and document the new 'override fires on parents too' contract in the public API/changelog, or revert.

issues.description: No stated specification for the new $ref-propagation algorithm; correctness rests on inline snapshots
issues.detail: The PR makes a substantive behavioral change to $ref/parent propagation in JSON Schema generation but does not state preconditions, postconditions, or invariants for flattenRef. Type narrowing of ref from `$ZodType | undefined | null` to `$ZodType | null` while parent is `$ZodType | undefined` is itself an inconsistency. The correctness argument is `toMatchInlineSnapshot`. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: Smuggled goto: `seen.ref = null` used as a mid-function recursion sentinel mutating shared state
issues.detail: The pattern `const ref = seen.ref; seen.ref = null; if (ref) { flattenRef(ref); ... }` is a flag mutating shared map state to break recursion — a goto in polite clothing. The same node is now reachable along both the ref edge and the parent edge, and the sentinel only blocks one. Replace with an explicit visited-set parameter and an invariant ('flattenRef is called at most once per (node, edge)'), or prove that mutating ctx.seen mid-traversal preserves invariants of every other consumer.

issues.description: Two near-identical dedup loops with copy-pasted skip guards
issues.detail: The block at ~418 (de-dup against refSeen.def) and the block at ~444 (de-dup against parentSeen.def) are the same loop written twice, including the same `if (key === "$ref" || key === "allOf") continue;` skip and the same JSON.stringify equality. Textbook special-case-instead-of-generalizing smell. Extract one helper `removeInheritedKeys(target, source)` and call it twice, or fix the underlying model so neither copy is needed.

issues.description: isParentRef branch deletes keys it did not add; invariant unstated and fragile
issues.detail: After `Object.assign(schema, refSchema); Object.assign(schema, _cached);` the `isParentRef` branch walks every key on schema and deletes anything not in `_cached`. `_cached` is a snapshot of `seen.def ?? seen.schema` from BEFORE the merge — so any property the child had implicitly (added by an earlier processor pass before flattenRef ran) gets stripped. The assumption 'child is a refinement so it inherits nothing' is doing a lot of work and is undocumented. State the loop invariant and the asymmetry with the non-parent branch, or don't reconstruct intent by set-difference.

issues.description: process() reorders parent handling without explaining the consequence to processors and traversal order
issues.detail: Previously, when a parent existed, the parent was processed first and the child's own processor was skipped. Now the child's processor always runs first, the parent is processed afterward, and result.ref is set only if the processor did not already set one. Processors that previously could assume 'my parent's seen.schema is populated when I run' no longer can; processors that set ref now race with the parent-link logic. The reversed iteration in the final loop (`[...ctx.seen.entries()].reverse()`) interacts with this. State the new invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Refinement detection couples constructor flag, process() copy, and finalize derivation across three hops
issues.detail: Classic schemas.ts adds `{ parent: true }` so the clone's _zod.parent points at the original. process() copies this into seen.parent. finalize() then re-derives 'is this a refinement' via `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref`. The information 'this edge is the parent edge' is already in seen.parent — recomputing it through an `as any` cast invites the two sources to disagree under cloning. Read from `seen.parent === ref` (drop the cast), or model the relationship explicitly on seen (e.g. seen.relationship: 'refinement' | 'wrapper' | 'inherited') set once at process time.

issues.description: Mini's check now sets parent: true with no test proving substitutability with classic
issues.detail: mini/schemas.ts uncomments `{ parent: true }` (previously deliberately commented out) and classic/schemas.ts adds the same flag. This is a postcondition strengthening for every caller relying on mini.check NOT establishing a parent link (anyone iterating _zod.parent chains, anyone depending on isParent not being set during JSON-Schema emission). No mini-side test demonstrates equivalence with classic on the new wrapper-id case. Either add a 'mini and classic produce identical JSON Schema for a check-augmented type' test, or document the divergence and justify why the prior comment-out has been forgotten.

issues.description: fileProcessor anyOf branches lose their standalone constraints; spec change is undocumented
issues.detail: The processor hoists shared props (type, format, contentEncoding, minLength, maxLength) to the root and reduces each anyOf branch to `{ contentMediaType: m }`. JSON Schema validators that interpret anyOf branches in isolation will see branches with no `type: string` constraint. Most validators merge with the root for draft 2020-12 — but this codebase explicitly handles draft 07/04 and OpenAPI 3.0 in flattenRef, and the postcondition 'value accepted iff string of right length/encoding with one of the listed mime types' was never written down. The typed return JSONSchema.StringSchema was also dropped from the map callback. Add the spec comment naming which target semantics this relies on, and a property test against the postcondition.

issues.description: Seen.ref type tightened from `$ZodType | undefined | null` to `$ZodType | null` while Seen.parent uses `undefined` for absence
issues.detail: Two adjacent fields now use opposite conventions for 'absent.' ref uses null as the 'already processed' sentinel and presumably also as 'never set' since undefined was removed; parent uses undefined. A reader cannot tell from the types which absence means what. With exactOptionalPropertyTypes, this also prevents explicit assignment of undefined to ref. Pick one convention, document the three-valued state on ref (unset / processing / done / ref(x)), or model with a discriminated union.

issues.description: Commented-out `// { parent: true }` in mini uncommented with no note explaining why it is now safe
issues.detail: The prior commented-out line presumably had a reason — likely 'this broke something, revisit'. The commit message does not say what changed that makes enabling it safe now (presumably the new parent-tracking path in finalize). A one-line comment or commit note would prevent the next maintainer from re-disabling for the same forgotten reason.

issues.description: fileProcessor refactor is a good simplification but worth naming the invariant in code
issues.detail: The change from 'put shared props in every anyOf branch' to 'hoist shared props to root, leave only the discriminating contentMediaType in anyOf' is genuinely simpler and the snapshot diff confirms it. Worth a one-line comment naming that invariant so a future contributor does not 'helpfully' put the shared props back in each branch, and so downstream tooling walking anyOf naively is not silently broken.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug (metadata and $ref propagation across clone chains) and that splitting Seen.ref from Seen.parent is the right instinct, but six reviewers independently flag the implementation as under-specified and over-complected. Strongest unanimous claims: (1) JSON.stringify is used as the dedup equality primitive in a hot loop — flagged by all six reviewers as wrong (Knuth/Hickey/Dijkstra call it P0, Liskov/Pike/Torvalds P1), (2) play.ts ships as a debug scratchpad with a relative src import — flagged by all six, (3) the overrideCount expectation silently doubled from 6 to 12 under a test still titled 'do not run on references,' indicating an undocumented public-contract change. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity of the flattenRef rewrite itself: Knuth and Dijkstra refuse it as P0 (no termination proof, no invariant, smuggled-goto sentinel via `seen.ref = null`), Hickey/Liskov frame it as architectural complecting/wrong-boundary at P0/P1, while Pike treats the underlying issue as a data-structure smell at P1 and Torvalds treats it primarily as bad taste plus three-patches-in-one. Recommended preconditions for merge: state the flattenRef invariant and termination measure, replace JSON.stringify equality with a defined structural predicate (or track key provenance at assignment), reconcile the override-on-parent semantics with the test name and the public API, add a mini-vs-classic equivalence test for the new parent:true flag, drop or relocate play.ts, and split the fileProcessor refactor into its own patch.
